newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: SLOW PROGRESS FOR THREDBO RESCUE WORKERS
Emergency Services teams working on clearing the Thredbo landslide site have made slow progress overnight, with lengthy disruptions caused by instability in the rubble.
Work stopped for three hours when movement was detected in one of the large concrete slabs from the collapsed ski lodges.
The official death toll remains at 10. There has been one survivor and eight people are still missing.
FISCHER, DEEK PRAISE FREEMAN'S VICTORY
Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer said Cathy Freeman had done the nation proud by winning gold in the 400-metre event at the World Championship meet in Athens.
"It is an outstanding effort," Mr Fischer said. "Congratulations from all Australians to Cathy Freeman on her splendid win.
"It's in the best traditions of Evonne Goolagong and many others."
The last Australian to win gold at a World Championship meet was Rob de Castella, who took the 1983 marathon title in Helsinki.
CABINET DEVOTES ITS ENERGIES TO UNEMPLOYMENT ISSUE
Federal Cabinet will devote its meeting today to unemployment, but it is unlikely to make any major announcements on the issue.
The meeting has been described as an information session, devoted to briefings on many aspects of the labour market and the general economy.
Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone said a number of papers would be discussed, but she sought to play down the importance of the meeting.
The Opposition called on Cabinet to come up with solutions, saying the community was sick of being told to be patient.
The Australian Business Chamber said the creation of more low-paying jobs was not the answer to the problem, and Cabinet should concentrate on creating career paths for workers.
CHANGES TO TAX ON PRIVATISED FACILITIES
The Federal Government has made a major change to the way it taxes public institutions after they're privatised.
The change could end up costing the states billions of dollars.
In an unexpected move, Treasurer Peter Costello has announced companies that buy privatised public assets will have to use a lower asset value to calculate depreciation rates than before.
In effect, firms that buy public assets like electricity companies and airports will have to pay higher rates of tax for the companies than previously.
HIGH COURT RULING ON STATE TAXES
Treasury officials around Australia are anxiously awaiting a High Court ruling this morning on a challenge to the States' and Territories' rights to tax tobacco, alcohol and petrol.
If the challenge under Section 90 of the Constitution is upheld, the Federal Government may impose higher taxes to cover revenue shortfalls from the states.
But if the Court interprets Section 90 more narrowly, it could open the way for wide-ranging state consumption taxes.
West Australian Premier Richard Court says there's a third possibility: a status quo decision, which would preserve the State's financial position, but stymie tax reform.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
